title: Match Group CEO: What Makes a Match on Tinder? | Podcast | In Good Company
description:
What actually makes two strangers match? Nicolai Tangen is joined by Spencer Rascoff, CEO of Match Group, the company behind Tinder, Hinge and a dozen other dating apps, for a conversation about how modern romance really works. They get into the algorithm doing the matchmaking, what separates a profile that works from one that doesn't, what Gen Z has changed about dating, and why loneliness has become such a big part of the story. Along the way, he shares what he's learned about building companies, and why Norway caught his attention. Tune in, this one's good fun!

In Good Company is hosted by Nicolai Tangen, CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management. New episode out every Wednesday.

The podcast In Good Company is part of Norges Bank Investment Management, a podcast about our investments. We are transparent about how the fund is invested. In this podcast, you get a deeper insight into the companies the fund is invested in.

Our CEO, Nicolai Tangen, has in-depth interviews with the leaders of some of the largest companies in the world. You will get insight into their leadership principles, the company’s strategy and how they are dealing with a large investor like us. You will also learn more about our role as an owner of the companies.

You can read more about the podcast on https://www.nbim.no/en/publications/podcast/
summary: Norges Bank Investment Management owns a 1% stake in Match Group, the parent company of Tinder and Hinge, and is highlighting the CEO's recent algorithmic improvements that unified recommendation decks to better personalize user matches. The podcast argues that while the company has significantly improved its matching quality over the last 18 months, there remains substantial potential for further growth, particularly with the upcoming implementation of real-time recommendation updates later this year.
